title: Construct Tree from Preorder + Inorder
description: Preorder gives roots in order; inorder splits left/right around each root. Recurse on the two halves, indexing inorder with a Map for O(n).

notes: The next unused preorder element is ALWAYS the root of the current inorder window — that is why a single moving pointer `p` suffices.
Build the left subtree before the right: preorder consumes left subtree entirely before the right root appears.
Without the inorder→index Map, finding `mid` costs O(n) per call → O(n^2) overall.

questions.q: Which preorder element is the root of the current subtree?
options: The middle of the preorder array

questions.q: Why must the left subtree be built before the right?
options: Preorder consumes the entire left subtree before reaching the right root
O(1) lookup of the root's split position, avoiding O(n^2) overall

questions.q: Time complexity of the Map-based solution?

blanks.hint: empty window when low passes high
left subtree ends just before mid
right subtree starts just after mid

L3.prompt: Write `buildTree(preorder, inorder)` returning the reconstructed binary tree. Log the post-order traversal as a JSON array for preorder=[3,9,20,15,7], inorder=[9,3,15,20,7].
hints: Move a single pointer through preorder; at each step it names the current root.
Use a Map from value → inorder index to split in O(1).
Recurse left then right; the preorder pointer naturally lines up.
